title: Genetic Analysis Reveals Population Expansion, Connectivity and Declining Genetic Diversity in Dory Snapper (Lutjanus fulviflamma) Along the Coastline of Tanzania
content:
ABSTRACT

In this study, genetic diversity, demographic history and population structure of Lutjanus fulviflamma were investigated using mtDNA COI sequence from 66 samples collected from six populations along the coastline of Tanzania. Samples were collected in 2024 from Tanga, Dar es Salaam, Mtwara and Mafia (Mainland Tanzania), and Unguja and Pemba (Zanzibar). Six haplotypes with an overall moderate haplotype (0.563) and low nucleotide (0.12%) diversities were obtained from 66 sequences. The negative overall Tajima's D (−1.24) and Fu's Fs (−1.66) values, Bayesian skyline plot and a unimodal mismatch distribution plot all suggested that L. fulviflamma may have experienced population bottlenecks followed by expansion in the recent history. AMOVA results showed high genetic variation within populations (88.47%) and low genetic variation among populations (11.53%), suggesting strong gene flow. The low FST fixation index value (0.11530) and a star-like haplotype network further supported the lack of genetic structure, indicating a single, genetically similar stock. These findings suggest the need for monitoring genetic diversity and population structure of commercially important fish species to guide sustainable fisheries management. Given their low genetic diversity, these populations are vulnerable to environmental changes and overfishing. Effective management strategies should focus on regulating fishing practices and protecting key habitats like seagrass beds and mangroves, which are important nurseries for juvenile L. fulviflamma.
